tutorial.welcome.title: WELCOME TO SKYRIMNET
tutorial.welcome.body: SkyrimNet makes every NPC in Skyrim into a real conversationalist. They hold their own opinions, remember what happened to them, react to what's going on around them, and decide what to do next — all voiced through the text-to-speech engine of your choice, all powered by your choice of large language model.
tutorial.discord.title: JOIN THE COMMUNITY
tutorial.discord.body: The SkyrimNet Discord is the primary hub for support, whether you need assistance with setup, guidance on configuring your models, or want to share your experiences with the community.
tutorial.login.title: Sign in to SkyrimNet
tutorial.login.body_not_ready: Account-based setup is coming soon. For now, continue to set things up manually.
tutorial.manual_setup.title: Manual Setup
tutorial.manual_setup.intro: First, we'll pick an AI provider and the large language models that you will use. Your provider is how SkyrimNet communicates with the AI to power its features. Large language models are what perform certain tasks like generating dialogue. OpenRouter is the recommended choice for new users.
tutorial.skip_confirm: Skip the tutorial? If you haven't at least configured your AI provider and models, SkyrimNet will not function. The tutorial can be restarted from the Settings page.
tutorial.provider_select.title: Choose an AI Provider
tutorial.provider_select.subtitle: Pick where your LLM requests will be routed. You can change this later.
tutorial.providers.openrouter.name: OpenRouter
tutorial.providers.openrouter.desc: Single account, hundreds of models from every major lab. Best starting point for most users.
tutorial.providers.nanogpt.name: NanoGPT
tutorial.providers.nanogpt.desc: Pay-as-you-go at provider cost, with an optional subscription that covers open-source model usage.
tutorial.providers.nvidia.name: Nvidia NIM
tutorial.providers.nvidia.desc: Nvidia-hosted open models. Free tier available with rate limits.
tutorial.providers.chutes.name: Chutes
tutorial.providers.chutes.desc: Decentralized compute network running open-source models.
tutorial.providers.custom.name: Custom Provider
tutorial.providers.custom.desc: Self-hosted vLLM, a regional proxy, or any other OpenAI-compatible endpoint. You'll enter the endpoint and API Key in the next step.
tutorial.provider_setup.title: Set up {{name}}
tutorial.provider_setup.openrouter.form_: Sign up at OpenRouter, create an API key, and add some credits to your account. $10 should be enough to get started. Enter your API Key below.
tutorial.provider_setup.nanogpt.form_bod: Requires a NanoGPT API key with available credits. Enter your API Key below.
tutorial.provider_setup.nvidia.form_body: Requires an Nvidia developer account. Enter your API Key below.
tutorial.provider_setup.chutes.form_body: Requires a Chutes account with available credits. Enter your API Key below.
tutorial.provider_setup.custom_body: Name your custom provider then enter your Endpoint and API Key (if required). Endpoints must be OpenAI-compatible and end in "/v1/chat/completions".
tutorial.provider_setup.custom_select_su: Pick one you've already configured, or add a new one.
tutorial.apikey_status.error: Couldn't verify: provider returned an error
tutorial.apikey_status.unsupported: Auto-test not available for this provider
tutorial.apikey_warn.title: API key didn't validate
tutorial.apikey_warn.body: The API key for this provider was rejected by the auth check. If you continue you'll likely hit errors on the model test step. Continue anyway?
tutorial.preset_select.title: Choose Your Models
tutorial.preset_select.body_intro: Now you will need to select which large language models SkyrimNet will use for its tasks. SkyrimNet provides recommended presets to get you up and running quickly. You may choose to manually select models for each task if you wish.
tutorial.preset_select.no_presets: No presets available for this provider.
tutorial.preset_select.manual_warn: Going manual means you're responsible for managing and updating your model selections. Presets get automatic updates when models change or are retired. Continue?
tutorial.llm_test.title: Test Your Models
tutorial.llm_test.body: Let's run a quick test to make sure everything is working before moving on. This will check that all models are communicating successfully.
tutorial.llm_test.fail_hint: One or more models couldn't be reached. Use Back to double-check your provider, API key, and model selections, then run the test again.
tutorial.llm_test.diag.auth: Authentication failed. Your API key is likely wrong or expired. Re-check it on the provider step.
tutorial.llm_test.diag.credits: Rejected for billing reasons. Your provider account may be out of credits.
tutorial.llm_test.diag.rate_limit: Rate limited by the provider. Wait a moment, then run the test again.
tutorial.llm_test.diag.not_found: Model not found. Its ID may be wrong or unavailable on this provider. Check your model selection.
tutorial.llm_test.diag.connection: Couldn't reach the provider. Check your internet connection and that the endpoint is correct.
tutorial.llm_test.diag.timeout: The request timed out. The provider may be slow or unreachable. Try again.
tutorial.llm_test.diag.server: The provider had a server error. This is usually temporary, so try again shortly.
tutorial.llm_test.diag.empty: The model returned an empty response. It may be overloaded or misconfigured. Try again or pick another model.
tutorial.llm_test.diag.bad_request: The provider rejected the request. The model name may be wrong for this provider, or one of its settings is not supported.
tutorial.llm_test.warn_body: One or more variants failed the test. You can continue, but those variants will fail at runtime until their provider/model is fixed. Continue anyway?
tutorial.tts_intro.title: Voice
tutorial.tts_intro.body: Next, we'll set up text-to-speech — how NPC dialogue is spoken aloud. SkyrimNet supports several text-to-speech engines, from free local ones like Piper to higher-quality cloud services like ElevenLabs. Pick whichever fits your hardware and budget; you can change it later from the Text-to-Speech page.
tutorial.tts_select.title: Choose a TTS Engine
tutorial.tts_select.subtitle: Each engine has its own trade-offs in quality, speed, cost, and hardware needs. You can change this later from the Text-to-Speech page.
tutorial.tts_select.engines.pockettts.de: Free neural TTS bundled with SkyrimNet. Voice cloning from short samples; runs on your CPU. Models download automatically on first use.
tutorial.tts_select.engines.piper.desc: Free, lightweight open-source TTS bundled with SkyrimNet. CPU-only and very fast. No voice cloning.
tutorial.tts_select.engines.inworld.desc: Cloud TTS built for games, with instant voice cloning. Subscription pricing.
tutorial.tts_select.engines.elevenlabs.d: Premium cloud TTS with the best overall quality. Paid subscription with usage-based billing.
tutorial.tts_select.engines.xtts.desc: Fast open-source voice-cloning TTS. Requires a local server or a server rented from VastAI.
tutorial.tts_select.engines.zonos.desc: Open-source TTS with emotion-aware voices. Requires a local server or a server rented from VastAI.
tutorial.tts_select.engines.chatterbox.d: Open-source voice-cloning TTS. Requires a GPU server to run.
tutorial.tts_select.engines.higgs.desc: Fast, high-quality audio model supporting 43 control tags for emotion, prosody, and style.
tutorial.tts_select.engines.openai_compa: Reusable voice cloning through Boson.ai Higgs 3 or a compatible local, network, or VastAI server.
tutorial.tts_select.engines.disabled.des: Turn voice output off entirely. NPCs will still produce dialogue text but nothing will be spoken aloud.
tutorial.tts_host_choice.title: Hosting {{name}}
tutorial.tts_host_choice.subtitle: This engine runs on a GPU server. You can host one yourself or rent one through Vast.ai.
tutorial.tts_host_choice.host.name: I'll host my own server
tutorial.tts_host_choice.host.desc: Run the engine on your own GPU or another machine on your network. You'll enter the endpoint URL on the next page. Advanced.
tutorial.tts_host_choice.rent.name: Rent a GPU from Vast.ai
tutorial.tts_host_choice.rent.desc: Vast.ai is a marketplace for cheap rented GPU instances. We'll guide you through API setup and create the instance for you.
tutorial.tts_vastai.title: Set up VastAI
tutorial.tts_vastai.status_error: Couldn't verify: Vast.ai returned an error
tutorial.tts_vastai.body: Sign up at vast.ai, top up a few dollars of credit, and create an API key from your account page. Paste it below and we'll create the instance for you.
tutorial.tts_vastai.api_key_hint: Find this under Account → API Keys at vast.ai.
tutorial.tts_vastai.success: Instance is starting. It usually takes a minute or two before it's reachable.
tutorial.tts_vastai.next_step_hint: You can monitor the instance from Tools > Vast AI Manager later. Continue to the engine setup page when ready.
tutorial.tts_setup.title: Set up {{name}}
tutorial.tts_setup.engines.pockettts.for: PocketTTS is bundled with SkyrimNet. No setup required.
tutorial.tts_setup.engines.piper.form_bo: Piper is bundled with SkyrimNet, but its voice models must be downloaded separately. Use the download link in the configuration card below and install them as a mod.
tutorial.tts_setup.engines.inworld.form_: Sign up at Inworld, create an API key and copy your Workspace ID. Paste both below.
tutorial.tts_setup.engines.elevenlabs.fo: Sign up at ElevenLabs and create an API key. Paste it below.
tutorial.tts_setup.engines.xtts.form_bod: XTTS runs on a GPU server. Run one locally, or rent one through Tools > Vast AI Manager (or use the button below).
tutorial.tts_setup.engines.zonos.form_bo: Zonos runs on a GPU server. Run one locally, or rent one through Tools > Vast AI Manager (or use the button below).
tutorial.tts_setup.engines.chatterbox.fo: Chatterbox runs on a GPU server. Paste the server URL below once it's running.
tutorial.tts_setup.engines.higgs.form_bo: Higgs runs on a local audio server or container. Paste the server URL below once it's running.
tutorial.tts_setup.engines.openai_compat: Choose Boson.ai Higgs 3 or a compatible self-hosted service. Self-hosted Higgs can run locally, on another computer, or through the VastAI preset below.
tutorial.tts_test.title: Test Your Voice
tutorial.tts_test.body: Now we will test your selected TTS engine to ensure it's working correctly. Enter a prompt below and click Test Voice.
tutorial.tts_test.diag.voice: The selected voice wasn't accepted. Its ID may be wrong or unavailable for this engine. Re-check the voice on the setup step.
tutorial.tts_test.diag.playback: The audio was generated but couldn't be played. Check your audio output device and volume.
tutorial.tts_test.diag.auth: Authentication failed. The engine's API key is likely wrong or expired. Re-check it on the setup step.
tutorial.tts_test.diag.credits: Rejected for billing reasons. Your TTS provider account may be out of credits or quota.
tutorial.tts_test.diag.rate_limit: Rate limited by the engine. Wait a moment, then run the test again.
tutorial.tts_test.diag.not_found: The engine endpoint or voice model wasn't found. Check the endpoint URL and voice selection on the setup step.
tutorial.tts_test.diag.connection: Couldn't reach the TTS engine. If it's a local engine, make sure its server is running; for a cloud or rented engine, check your internet and the endpoint.
tutorial.tts_test.diag.timeout: Generation timed out. A local engine may still be loading its model, or a remote one may be slow. Try again.
tutorial.tts_test.diag.server: The engine returned a server error. This is usually temporary, so try again shortly.
tutorial.tts_test.diag.empty: The engine returned no audio. It may be misconfigured or still warming up. Try again or pick another engine.
tutorial.tts_test.diag.bad_request: The engine rejected the request. A voice or generation setting may be invalid for this engine.
tutorial.tts_test.warn_body: The last test failed. You can continue, but voice will not work in-game until the engine config is fixed. Continue anyway?
tutorial.stt_intro.title: Microphone Input
tutorial.stt_intro.body: Now, we'll set up speech-to-text — how SkyrimNet listens to you when you talk to NPCs. You can run a local Whisper model, point at an external Whisper-compatible API, or skip voice input entirely and use text input instead.
tutorial.stt_select.title: Choose a Speech-to-Text Backend
tutorial.stt_select.subtitle: Pick how your microphone audio gets transcribed. You can change this later from the Speech-to-Text page.
tutorial.stt_select.backends.whisper.des: Free open-source Whisper model running locally on your CPU or GPU. Models download on first use.
tutorial.stt_select.backends.external_wh: Point at any OpenAI-compatible Whisper API endpoint. Requires an endpoint; hosted providers such as OpenAI or OpenRouter also need an API key.
tutorial.stt_select.backends.disabled.de: Turn microphone input off entirely. You'll still be able to type to NPCs. You can enable a backend later from the Speech-to-Text page.
tutorial.stt_setup.title: Set up {{name}}
tutorial.stt_setup.backends.whisper.form: Pick a model size in the configuration below — smaller models are faster but less accurate. Use the download button next to the dropdown to fetch the model if you don't have it yet.
tutorial.stt_setup.backends.external_whi: Enter the API endpoint and key for your Whisper provider, plus the model name. The default is OpenRouter ("openai/whisper-1"); for OpenAI use https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions with "whisper-1".
tutorial.stt_test.title: Test Your Microphone
tutorial.stt_test.body: Click the button and speak for up to {{seconds}} seconds. The backend will transcribe what you said to confirm that your mic and model are working.
tutorial.stt_test.no_speech: No speech detected in the recording.
tutorial.stt_test.error_no_result: Transcription timed out. The backend didn't return a result.
tutorial.stt_test.diag.mic: No microphone was available. Check that a mic is plugged in, set as your default recording device, and that Skyrim is allowed to use it.
tutorial.stt_test.diag.model: The Whisper model isn't ready. Use the download button on the setup step to fetch it, then try again.
tutorial.stt_test.diag.auth: Authentication failed. Your Whisper API key is likely wrong or expired. Re-check it on the setup step.
tutorial.stt_test.diag.credits: Rejected for billing reasons. Your transcription provider account may be out of credits or quota.
tutorial.stt_test.diag.rate_limit: Rate limited by the provider. Wait a moment, then record again.
tutorial.stt_test.diag.not_found: The transcription endpoint or model wasn't found. Check the endpoint URL and model name on the setup step.
tutorial.stt_test.diag.connection: Couldn't reach the transcription backend. For an external API, check your internet and the endpoint URL.
tutorial.stt_test.diag.timeout: Transcription timed out. The backend may be slow or still loading its model. Try again.
tutorial.stt_test.diag.server: The transcription backend returned a server error. This is usually temporary, so try again shortly.
tutorial.stt_test.diag.empty: The backend returned no transcription. It may be misconfigured or still loading its model. Try again.
tutorial.stt_test.diag.bad_request: The backend rejected the request. The model name or a setting may be invalid for this provider.
tutorial.stt_test.warn_body: The last test failed. You can continue, but speech-to-text won't work in-game until the backend config is fixed. Continue anyway?
tutorial.hotkey_intro.title: Hotkeys
tutorial.hotkey_intro.body: SkyrimNet uses hotkeys to open the chat input, use push-to-talk, open the dashboard, and trigger a handful of other actions. In the next step you may rebind or unset any of SkyrimNet's hotkeys. Not all hotkeys are required.
tutorial.hotkey_setup.body: Click any key chip to rebind it. Anything you don't change stays at its default.
tutorial.hotkey_setup.body_input: These are how you will communicate in SkyrimNet. Not all of them are required. You can also use the Wheel Menu on the next page instead of individual keybinds.
tutorial.hotkey_setup.body_ui: These allow you to access the Wheel Menu or Dashboard in-game. The Wheel Menu can execute many different SkyrimNet functions with a single key.
tutorial.hotkey_setup.body_toggles: These are basic toggles for a few different SkyrimNet features. All of these can also be toggled within the Dashboard or Wheel Menu.
tutorial.hotkey_setup.body_actions: These keybinds execute various SkyrimNet functions. All of these are optional, but Capture Crosshair is required to use the OmniSight feature's NPC descriptions.
tutorial.load_order.title: Plugins for Your Mods
tutorial.load_order.intro: SkyrimNet's plugin hub carries content written for specific mods — character bios, triggers, prompts and more. These ones match the mods already in your load order. Install the bio packs now, or skip and browse them later from the Plugins page.
tutorial.load_order.empty: Nothing in the hub matches your load order yet. You can browse everything from the Plugins page once setup finishes.
tutorial.final_intro.title: Almost Done
tutorial.final_intro.body: Just one final step. SkyrimNet needs to know who you are. On the next two pages, we'll review a handful of player-specific options — like whether your character will generate their own thoughts and memories and what voice type they will use. Then you'll write a short bio describing your character. The bio is what other characters know about you when they meet you.
tutorial.player_settings.title: Player Options
tutorial.player_settings.body: These settings affect only your character. You can change any of them later from Characters > Player Settings.
tutorial.player_bio.title: Write Your Character Bio
tutorial.player_bio.body: Bios are separated into blocks governing different subjects. Summary and Appearance are what NPCs will see when speaking with you. The other blocks determine how your character will roleplay. You may use the Update Bio button to have an AI assist you with writing your bio. It is recommended to have a save loaded for this step.
tutorial.player_bio.update_hint: Have the AI revise your current bio based on a free-text instruction ("make her more cynical", "add a Whiterun backstory", …).
tutorial.complete.title: You're Ready to Play
tutorial.complete.body: SkyrimNet is ready to go. There are many more ways to customize SkyrimNet, but this is enough to get you started. Click Finish to access the rest of the dashboard, or Feature Guide to see an overview of SkyrimNet's features.
tutorial.complete.line_player: Player options and character bio saved
tutorial.fo_prompts.title: Prompts
tutorial.fo_prompts.intro: Prompts are how SkyrimNet provides instructions to the LLM to guide roleplay. Character bios, world settings, response behavior, and more are all defined through individual prompt files. These files can be freely edited to tailor SkyrimNet to your preferences. Below is an example world setting prompt:
tutorial.fo_prompts.outro: SkyrimNet uses Inja syntax and decorators for pulling game data and conditional logic into prompts.
tutorial.fo_prompts.editor_hint: Describe how your Skyrim plays. This text is added to every conversation.
tutorial.fo_bios.title: Character Bios
tutorial.fo_bios.intro: SkyrimNet gives the player and each NPC a bio: a structured profile the LLM reads before deciding what they say or do. Each bio is split into blocks, and each block governs one part of who the character is. You wrote your own during setup, and you can edit any character's bio from the Characters page. Generic and modded NPCs may not have a bio by default, but you can create one for them from the Characters page.
tutorial.fo_bios.block.summary: A concise summary of the character's role, personality, and primary traits.
tutorial.fo_bios.block.interject_summary: A description of what topics or themes would motivate them to join conversations.
tutorial.fo_bios.block.background: A narrative highlighting essential background details relevant to their current role.
tutorial.fo_bios.block.personality: A description of personality, core values, emotional tone, biases, and typical behavior.
tutorial.fo_bios.block.appearance: Brief description emphasizing distinguishing physical traits, appearance, and presentation.
tutorial.fo_bios.block.aspirations: A short list of long-term goals or critical motivations.
tutorial.fo_bios.block.relationships: Bullet points listing key relationships and a short description of the relationship.
tutorial.fo_bios.block.occupation: A description of essential job functions, daily routines, and typical activities.
tutorial.fo_bios.block.skills: Bullet list of relevant practical skills and capabilities directly useful in interactive scenarios.
tutorial.fo_bios.block.speech_style: Instructions on speaking style, tone, mannerisms, and emotional delivery.
tutorial.fo_bios.outro: Summary and appearance are what others perceive at a glance; the rest shapes how a character thinks and roleplays. Bios can also be updated dynamically to reflect recent events and changes.
tutorial.fo_ve.title: Virtual Entities
tutorial.fo_ve.intro: Not every character needs a body. A virtual entity is a presence with a bio and a voice but no actor in the world: a deity you pray to, a spirit, or the voice in your head. Virtual Entities can be created from the Characters page. For example, a Daedric Prince you can speak to:
tutorial.fo_ve.outro: Because a virtual entity is just a bio and a voice, you can give any idea a presence in your world: a god who answers prayers, a ghost that lingers, or a conscience that talks back.
tutorial.fo_omnisight.title: OmniSight
tutorial.fo_omnisight.intro: OmniSight gives SkyrimNet eyes. It captures what's on screen and turns it into a written description of the scene, so characters know where they are and what surrounds them, not just who they're talking to. OmniSight can also capture and generate descriptions of actors, equipment, and items. Screenshots are stored locally and converted to text by an LLM.
tutorial.fo_omnisight.image_alt: An in-game Skyrim screenshot captured by OmniSight
tutorial.fo_omnisight.example:
A wooden bridge crosses a calm river, its planks and railings supported by stone foundations. The bridge leads toward a cluster of rustic wooden structures with thatched roofs, situated on the far bank. The immediate foreground features a gravel path bordered by grass, wildflowers, and scattered boulders. Tall, leafy deciduous trees line the riverbanks and surround the settlement, while large, moss-covered rocks are prominent near the water’s edge. In the distance, misty, snow-capped mountains rise above the treeline, partially obscured by low-hanging clouds. 

This is a small riverside settlement nestled in a forested valley. The visible architecture suggests a modest, functional community built around the river, with buildings connected by wooden walkways. The presence of multiple structures and the bridge imply a hub for crossing the water, likely serving as a local waypoint or outpost. The overall atmosphere is one of quiet, rural isolation, framed by the natural grandeur of the surrounding wilderness.
tutorial.fo_omnisight.outro: With a sense of place, characters can react to the world itself: a fortress on the horizon, a storm rolling in, or a body lying in the road.
tutorial.fo_events.title: Events
tutorial.fo_events.intro: SkyrimNet records what happens in-game as text and sends it to the LLM to provide context. Events include vanilla dialogue, AI-generated speech, trades, and more, each one tagged with the actors involved, the location, and the time. Events inform the responses, memories, and actions of the characters around you. They can be viewed, edited, or deleted from the Events or Home pages.
tutorial.fo_events.ev1.content: Everything's for sale, my friend. Everything.
tutorial.fo_events.ev2.content: John Skyrim completed a trade with Belethor. Bought 1x ABCs for Barbarians. Spent 7 gold.
tutorial.fo_events.ev3.content: John Skyrim read the book "ABCs for Barbarians".
tutorial.fo_events.outro: SkyrimNet saves thousands of events for a comprehensive history of your game, though the LLM only sees the most recent ones. Events are condensed into memories for long-term history.
tutorial.fo_memories.title: Memories
tutorial.fo_memories.intro: SkyrimNet generates memories for NPCs after your interactions to be retrieved later. They summarize the events that took place and how the NPC felt about it in first-person. Every NPC has its own unique memories — one interaction may be impactful to one person, but forgettable to another. Relevant memories are looked up and sent as context with every dialogue exchange so NPCs remember what you're talking about.
tutorial.fo_memories.m1.content: Sold a copy of "ABCs for Barbarians" to a wanderer called John Skyrim. Seven gold, no haggling, bless him. Odd thing for a sellsword to want, but I never argue with good coin. If he reads as eagerly as he buys, he'll be back.
tutorial.fo_memories.m2.content: Carlotta had her cart out before the gates even opened, parked right in the path of the morning crowd. She gave me that little wave, friendly as you please. We are not friends. One slow week and I'll undercut her on apples until she packs up for good.
tutorial.fo_memories.outro: Memories capture moments one at a time; a diary takes the wider view, looking back over a whole day and setting it down in the character's own words.
tutorial.fo_diaries.title: Diaries
tutorial.fo_diaries.intro: SkyrimNet can generate a diary entry for any character: a longer, first-person account of their recent experiences, typically covering an entire day, written in their own voice. Unlike memories, diaries aren't created automatically; they have to be created with a button press or a trigger. Entries are saved per character and can be read, edited, or voiced from the Diary page, and each new one picks up from the last.
tutorial.fo_diaries.content:
Another of those grey, half-empty mornings where the only sound is my own broom and the creak of the sign over the door. The dust on the high shelves has settled so thick it is starting to look like inventory of its own, and gods help me, I half wondered if I could move it as powdered something-or-other to the right fool. Carlotta had her cart out before the gate guards had finished yawning, skimming off what little foot traffic a Last Seed morning brings, and then she had the gall to wave at me across the square, bright as a new septim. We are not friends. We are two people smiling at one another while we pick each other's pockets, and we both know it.

Trade found me past noon, at least. A wanderer wandered in, a big fellow with a sword on his back and a name like a tavern boast, John Skyrim. He had that look the adventuring sort always wear, wide-eyed and restless, like the whole world is just a barrow waiting to be cracked open and tipped out for its coin. I had him pegged for a blade or a healing draught. Instead he drifted to the shelf in the corner and came back with a copy of *ABCs for Barbarians*, of all the things on the gods' green Nirn. Seven gold, I told him, and he did not so much as blink. Seven. I would have let it walk for five and called myself shrewd for the trouble. Lesson noted, and underlined: next time I start at nine and let them haggle me down to seven. The bookish ones never argue the price. They are too embarrassed to be caught wanting the thing in the first place, and embarrassment, I have learned, is worth a good two or three septims a sale.

The caravan from Solitude is late again, the third time this month, and my patience is thinner than my stock. If it has been jumped on the road, that is a week of goods I will never see and a loss I have no intention of swallowing myself. I will send word in the morning. Politely. The kind of polite that means *pay me*, written in a hand pleasant enough that no one could ever prove I meant it as a threat.

But the coin is counted, the door is barred, the lamp is turned down low, and the day ends a few septims heavier than it began. That is the whole of it, in the end. Let Carlotta have her mornings. Let the heroes go chasing their barrows. I will be right here, behind this counter, where the world comes to me and pays for the privilege.
tutorial.fo_diaries.outro: Memories and diaries are personal accounts bound to one person. The setting prompt holds global facts, but World Knowledge lets certain NPCs be aware of specific things.
tutorial.fo_wk.title: World Knowledge
tutorial.fo_wk.intro: World knowledge exposes facts to specific NPCs or groups through conditions, like belonging to a faction or a quest reaching a certain stage. You write entries yourself or import packs shared by the community. The AI Assistant can also aid in the creation of knowledge entries. Knowledge is tied to your save and pulled into conversations semantically when relevant, so it doesn't clutter context with lore that doesn't apply. Alternatively, important facts can always be injected into the context.
tutorial.fo_wk.wk1.title: Whiterun has fallen
tutorial.fo_wk.wk1.content: The Stormcloaks have taken Whiterun. Imperial banners are down and Jarl Balgruuf has fled the city.
tutorial.fo_wk.wk2.title: The attack on Helgen
tutorial.fo_wk.wk2.content: A dragon attacked Helgen and razed it. Few survived, and rumors of the beast are spreading across the holds.
tutorial.fo_wk.wk3.title: The Companions' secret
tutorial.fo_wk.wk3.content: The inner circle of the Companions are secretly werewolves, a truth they guard closely.
tutorial.fo_wk.outro: Each entry is either always injected whenever its condition passes, or pulled in semantically when the conversation is relevant. Quest-critical facts stay in scope, while incidental lore only surfaces when it matters.
tutorial.fo_gm.title: GameMaster
tutorial.fo_gm.intro: The GameMaster periodically evaluates the scene and decides whether to make an NPC speak, on a cooldown you can configure. It has two actions available: start a new conversation between nearby characters, or continue one already in progress. This lets NPCs keep talking on their own, rather than only speaking when the player does.
tutorial.fo_gm.start.desc: Picks an NPC to open a new exchange with someone nearby, bringing up a fresh topic.
tutorial.fo_gm.continue.desc: Picks an NPC to carry the current conversation forward.
tutorial.fo_gm.continuous_desc: Continuous mode causes the GameMaster to run faster to keep the conversation flowing. It needs to be toggled manually with a hotkey (F10 by default).
tutorial.fo_gm.outro: Start Conversation and Continue Conversation are two of SkyrimNet's actions. Actions are the full set of things characters can do in the world.
tutorial.fo_actions.title: Actions
tutorial.fo_actions.intro: Actions let NPCs do things in the game beyond speaking, like renting you an inn room, opening a trade window, or following you. Individual actions can be toggled on or off to control your desired behavior. SkyrimNet ships with several actions and many more can be downloaded from the community.
tutorial.fo_actions.outro: Custom actions can be created from quest scripts by browsing the Game Data Explorer in the dashboard.
tutorial.fo_triggers.title: Triggers
tutorial.fo_triggers.intro: Triggers fire a response whenever a particular in-game event occurs. A response can be dialogue, narration, dynamic bio updates, enabling virtual entities, and more. SkyrimNet doesn't include any triggers by default, but you can create them yourself or download them from the community. Below is an example that generates a player diary when you go to sleep.
tutorial.fo_triggers.outro: Triggers can be created manually from the Triggers page, or automatically from the Game Data Explorer and Event Monitor.
tutorial.fo_bards.title: Bard Singing
tutorial.fo_bards.intro: Bards or the player can compose and perform original songs using AI. The lyrics are drawn from recent events and NPC memory, then a music provider turns them into a sung performance. Bards will auto-perform when you enter an inn. Pick a provider and enter an API key, then click Test to hear a sample.
tutorial.fo_bards.outro: Generated songs are collected on the Bard Singing page, where you can browse and replay them.
tutorial.fo_ut.title: Universal Translator
tutorial.fo_ut.intro: The Universal Translator rewrites vanilla dialogue with the AI. You write a rule, a speech pattern for an NPC, faction, or race, and their stock lines come out transformed, whether that means a new accent, a different personality, or another language entirely.
tutorial.fo_ut.vanilla: I used to be an adventurer like you, then I took an arrow in the knee.
tutorial.fo_ut.r1.line: Aye, I swung steel for coin once, same as you. Then a stray arrow found my knee, and that was the end of it.
tutorial.fo_ut.r2.line: J'étais un aventurier comme toi, jusqu'à ce qu'une flèche vienne se loger dans mon genou.
tutorial.fo_ut.outro: Rules apply globally or to a specific NPC, faction, or race, and are set up on the Universal Translator page. Voicing silent NPCs requires DBVO to be installed.
tutorial.fo_wiki.title: Learn More
tutorial.fo_wiki.intro: For more detail on each feature, the SkyrimNet Wiki has in-depth guides, configuration options, and examples for each feature. You can access it any time from the dashboard's Wiki section or the link below.
